104	## 3. Known broken things (all upstream Medusa, not our fork)
105	
106	Our fork only adds STUDENTS.md and course files on top of Medusa 2.17.2. These are real upstream bugs.
107	
108	**1. 467 unit tests fail on a clean checkout.** `@medusajs/icons` 464/464 and `@medusajs/ui` 3/40.
109	All from one cause: `packages/design-system/icons/package.json` declares
110	`react: "^18.3.1 || ^19.0.0"` in devDependencies, so Yarn nests react@19.2.6 inside that package
111	while `react-dom@18.3.1` stays hoisted at root. React 19 elements + React 18 renderer =
112	"Objects are not valid as a React child". Fix: scoped resolution `"@medusajs/icons/react": "^18.3.1"`
113	in root package.json — precedent already exists there for `@redocly/cli/react`.
114	**68 of 70 packages pass.** Confirmed by three of us independently. NOT your machine.
115	
116	**2. The standalone dashboard dev server renders a blank page.**
117	`packages/admin/dashboard/vite.config.mts` defines only 3 of the 6 globals the source needs.
118	Missing: `__AUTH_TYPE__`, `__JWT_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY__`, `__MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE__`.
119	`src/lib/client/client.ts:3` throws a ReferenceError before React mounts. The bundled admin at
120	:9000 works because `admin-bundler/src/utils/config.ts:52-57` defines all six. Config was last
121	touched 2024-10-09; the source added those globals in late 2025. Nobody has fixed it.
122	Workaround already in the repo: `vi.hoisted()` in three spec files sets the globals for tests.
123	
124	**3. Form validation errors never display anywhere in the dashboard.**
125	`@hookform/resolvers@3.4.2` with `zod@4.2.0`. Resolvers v3 doesn't understand zod 4 errors, so
126	instead of putting them in form state it throws. **116 files use zodResolver, 104 render
127	`<Form.ErrorMessage />`, and none of them can show anything.** Submitting an invalid form just
128	silently refuses. Verified by running validation directly: errors exist with messages, they just
129	never reach the form.

182	**#58 in one paragraph (I get asked about this):** completing a cart when an item sold out returned
183	a 400 with no cart, so the storefront could not show which item was the problem. The error comes
184	from `ensureInventoryLevels` in the inventory module, thrown as `NOT_ALLOWED`. The promotion-limit
185	and subscription errors from the same workflow are also `NOT_ALLOWED`, so the route could not branch
186	on type. I attached the existing `INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY` code to the error at its source and added
187	a `statusOKErrorCodes` list to `packages/medusa/src/api/store/carts/[id]/complete/route.ts`.
188	Rejected alternatives: allow the whole `NOT_ALLOWED` type (swallows the other two), pre-check stock
189	(extra query on every checkout and still racy), new error type (the HTTP error handler does not know
190	it, so other routes 500). Cost: handled errors now live in two lists, and the code appears in other
191	routes' error bodies, which required updating two reservation tests.

254	## 9. Lessons learned
255	
256	Medusa core is deliberately minimal; the plugin ecosystem fills feature gaps. **Before proposing
257	anything, search externally, not just the repo.** Ideas that looked like gaps but already exist as
258	official or community plugins: Shopify migration (Medusa's own MCP server does it), sales analytics
259	dashboard (Agilo and rsc-labs plugins), abandoned cart recovery (community plugin + Medusa guide).
260	
261	The proposals that survive are ones a plugin **cannot** add — engine behavior, admin API routes,
262	core defaults. That's why #16 and #23 hold up.
263	
264	Also verified as genuinely missing: order CSV import (products have import+export, orders have
265	export only), customer export, and **a count of how many times a product has sold** —
266	`order_line_item` has indexed `product_id` and `variant_id` plus `quantity`, so the data is there
267	and indexed; nobody surfaced it. That last one is a natural sequel to #9 (order count + lifetime
268	spend for customers, which lefecko already merged).
269	
270	From Sprint 1:
271	- **Read the code before trusting an issue's scope.** #32 already existed, #16 was smaller than written.
272	- **Claim issues and get spec review comments at the start of the sprint.** Sprint 1 all landed on the last day.
273	- **Never paste issue/PR text copied from the terminal.** It mangled #32 and #40 twice. Save to a file and
274	  post with `gh issue edit N --body-file <file>` / `gh pr create --body-file <file>`.
275	- **Run parallel work in separate git worktrees**: `git worktree add ~/medusa-<n> -b <branch> origin/develop`.
276	- **Watch AI scope creep.** On #11 it added a whole-number rule for weights nobody asked for. Tell it to stick to
277	  the acceptance criteria and check commit messages before every commit.
278	
279	From Sprint 2:
280	- **Sprint 0 lost D4/D5 points because no issue comment linked the logs.** The link has to open the
281	  log file itself, not the folder. One "AI Assistance" comment per contributor per issue.
282	- **The error you are looking for is often not where the obvious code is.** On #58 I assumed
283	  `confirm-inventory.ts` because it already used `INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY`. That step does not run on
284	  cart completion at all. Trace the real path before designing.
285	- **Tag an error at its source, match on the tag at the boundary.** Beats pattern-matching messages
286	  or widening a type list that other errors share.
287	- **Every PR needs the Tech Debt section**, split into Introduced (a tradeoff you chose) and
288	  Encountered (pre-existing, scoped out). Sprint 3 adds Test Evidence on top of it.
289	- **Reviews must be substantive.** On #89 I checked out the branch, ran it, and reverted the author's
290	  fix to confirm his new test actually failed. That is the kind of thing worth writing down in the
291	  review.
292	- **Diagrams need a legend and annotations or they lose points**, even when the structure is right.

320	## 11. Conventions to follow
321	
322	- Prettier: no semicolons, double quotes, 2-space indent, ES5 trailing commas. `npx prettier --check <files>`
323	- Files kebab-case, types PascalCase, functions camelCase, constants SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, DB fields snake_case
324	- Commit style is mixed on the team: conventional (`feat(dashboard): ...`) and plain imperative both appear
325	- **Changesets required** — add one as a separate `chore:` commit. See `.changeset/` for format
326	- PR description format: What / Why / How / Testing, in plain prose, first person. Include the
327	  command to run the tests. No checklists, no bolded headers — teammates don't use them
328	- `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailers appear on some commits (lefecko uses them, upstream Medusa
329	  does too). Not required
330	- AI logs go to `ai-logs/sprint<N>/<username>/YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`. Link the log from
331	  the issue or PR it documents, as a full URL that opens the file itself, not the folder
332	- My commits: short plain subject only ("Add ...", "Fix ..."), no body, no Co-Authored-By line
333	- Every PR gets a teammate review with the course rubric. **Never self-approve or self-merge**
334	
335	**New in Sprint 3 (see `sprint3.md` for the full text):**
336	- Every PR description needs a **Test Evidence** table (one row per AC: test, level, source of the
337	  expected value) on top of the Tech Debt section. The source of an expected value may never be
338	  "what the code currently returns"
339	- A PR merges only after a teammate approves **the latest commit**. Pushing after an approval
340	  invalidates it
341	- A **spec review comment on the issue, before coding**, that states what the reviewer checked
342	- Use `Closes #<issue>` in the PR description and attach issues and PRs to the sprint milestone
343	- D6 mutation testing uses **StrykerJS** (Jest runner for backend packages, Vitest runner for the
344	  dashboard), run only on the files the PR changed, with before/after JSON reports committed
345

133	## Things that must improve from Sprint 2
134	
135	1. **Open PRs early.** In Sprint 2 most PRs were opened in the last two days, leaving no time for
136	   review. Sprint 3 needs a code PR by the mid-sprint check-in (D7).
137	
138	2. **Independent approval before merging.** A PR is merged only after a teammate approves **its
139	   latest commit**. Merging without an approval, or after pushing new commits since the approval,
140	   is not allowed. Once approved, the author may merge. Request the review on GitHub and notify the
141	   reviewer on Zulip; reviewers respond (approve or request changes) within 24 hours.
142	
143	3. **Spec reviews must be visible and show what was checked.** Before coding starts, a teammate
144	   posts a review comment **on the issue itself**. The comment states what the reviewer checked:
145	   whether each acceptance criterion is clear and testable, which cases were considered (and
146	   whether they are covered), and whether the scope fits. If there are problems, the reviewer lists
147	   them and the author updates the spec. "Looks good!" with nothing about what was checked is not
148	   acceptable.
149	
150	4. **Link PRs and issues.** Every code PR links the issue it addresses. Use `Closes #<issue>` in the
151	   PR description. Attach issues and code PRs to the Sprint 3 milestone.
152	
153	5. **AI logs must be real logs.** Prompts and the AI's output (SpecStory recommended). Not accepted:
154	   summaries of a session, paraphrased prompts, a share link to a chat, or tool output without the
155	   prompts that produced it. File names: `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`. Link the log from the
156	   issue or PR it documents.
157	
158	6. **The sprint report must render.** Check tables and links display correctly on GitHub (no escaped
159	   `\|` or `\[`). Use the Sprint 3 sections, not a copy of a previous report.

174	| Each CSCI 435 member | at least 2 medium issues (or equivalent story points) |
175	| **Each CSCI 535 (grad) member** | **at least 2 medium issues + 1 additional small issue** |
176	
177	**Scope must be justified.** Each issue states its scope (small or medium) and one or two sentences
178	on why: which components it touches and how much change is expected. The instructor or TA may
179	reclassify an issue whose scope is clearly overstated.
180	
181	**Hardening issues (optional).** One of your issues may be a hardening issue: work that makes the
182	existing system more reliable rather than adding a feature. Good sources:
183	- The baseline run (D8): failing tests, flaky tests, broken CI checks on the default branch
184	- Tech debt recorded in the "Introduced" and "Encountered" fields of Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 PRs
185	- Known bugs found in reviews, after merging, or by teammates
186	- The upstream issue tracker, for bugs in the parts of the system the team works on
187	
188	A hardening issue is scoped like any other issue and **must include evidence that the problem is
189	fixed**:
190	- **Bug fix:** a test that fails before the fix and passes after
191	- **Flaky test:** the root cause, plus enough repeated runs before and after to show the change
192	  (for example 20 runs for a unit test, 10 for an E2E test)
193	- **Broken or missing CI check:** links to CI runs before and after
194	- **Failing tests in the baseline:** pass/fail counts before and after, and the cause of each group
195	
196	Regenerating snapshots, reformatting code, or silencing a check without fixing its cause counts as
197	**small at most**.
198	
199	**Team feature.** When posted, split it into sub-issues, each with its own owner, spec (D2) and
200	scope. Link each sub-issue to the feature issue. Sub-issues count toward the scope minimum. Add the
201	sub-issues to the Sprint 3 milestone and adjust the backlog.
202	
203	Create a Sprint 3 milestone in GitHub and attach all selected issues.

205	**What to provide in D8:** link to the Sprint 3 milestone and the rationale for backlog decisions.

220	### D4 - Code Changes and Pull Requests (20 pts, individual)
221	
222	Same workflow as Sprint 2, **including the Tech Debt section**. Sprint 3 adds a **Test Evidence**
223	section to every PR description. It replaces the "how it was tested" part of the description, so
224	you don't write it twice.
225	
226	```markdown
227	## Test Evidence
228	
229	| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
230	|---|---|---|---|
231	| AC1: ... | ... | ... | ... |
232	
233	**Not tested automatically, and why:** [...]
234	
235	**AI-written tests:** [Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you
236	checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None."]
237	```
238	
239	**How to fill it in:**
240	- One row per acceptance criterion from D2. For bug reports, use the Expected Behavior instead. For
241	  PRs that change no product behavior (for example CI changes), write "N/A" and explain why.
242	- **Test(s):** the test name (and file, if not obvious). If checked manually, write `Manual:`
243	  followed by the steps and what you saw. If an AC is tested both ways, list both in the same row.
244	- **Level:** `unit`, `integration`, `E2E`, or `manual`.
245	- **Source of expected value:** where the expected result comes from. One of: `AC`,
246	  `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or `other` (explain). **The current output of
247	  your own code is not a valid source**; a test whose expected value was copied from what the code
248	  returns cannot detect that the code is wrong.
249	- **Not tested automatically, and why:** only for ACs checked manually only.
250	- You may use AI to draft this section, but you are responsible for checking that it is accurate.
251	
252	**Example:**
253	
254	| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
255	|---|---|---|---|
256	| AC1: An end date before the start date is rejected with an error | `outOfOffice.schema.test.ts > rejects end before start` | unit | AC |
257	| AC2: The away badge appears on the booking page during the out-of-office window | `booking-ooo.e2e.ts > shows away badge in window` | E2E | AC |
258	| AC3: The badge text is readable in dark mode | Manual: enabled dark mode, opened the booking page during the window, badge text is readable | manual | issue discussion |
259	
260	**Not tested automatically, and why:** AC3 depends on visual contrast, which our test setup does not check.
261	
262	**If your fork has no CI that runs your tests** (ours does not run on PRs), include the command(s)
263	you ran and a summary of the results (passed, failed, skipped).
264	
265	**Reviewers add one line to the code review rubric** (from Sprint 1 D4):
266	
267	| Criterion | Score (1-10) | Notes |
268	|---|---|---|
269	| Test evidence - does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally? | | |

277	### D6 - Mutation Testing (15 pts, individual) - NEW
278	
279	**What it is.** A mutation testing tool makes small changes to your code (**mutants**), such as
280	flipping a condition or changing a boundary value, and runs your tests against each one. If a test
281	fails, the mutant is **killed**. If all tests pass, the mutant **survived**: your tests did not
282	notice that the code changed. Survivors point to weak or missing tests.
283	
284	**What to do.** For one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests
285	(**CSCI 535: two such issues**; your small issue may be one of them):
286	
287	1. Run a mutation testing tool **on the source files changed by your PR(s) for that issue**. Do not
288	   run it on the whole project.
289	2. Using the tool's report, **analyze every surviving mutant**: is it **equivalent** (it behaves
290	   exactly like the original code, so no test can kill it), or does it reveal a **gap** in your
291	   tests? If there are more than 10 survivors, analyze at least 10, starting with those in lines
292	   your PR added or changed.
293	3. **Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a surviving mutant** that revealed a gap.
294	   Re-run the tool to confirm it is killed. If no survivor reveals a gap (all killed or equivalent),
295	   say so and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
296	4. Answer the questions in the template.
297	
298	**Evidence.** Configure the tool to write a machine-readable report (**StrykerJS: add `"json"` to
299	`reporters`**). Commit the report from the first run and the re-run as
300	`docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json` and `-after.json`. The mutation
301	scores you list must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in
302	the "after" report.
303	
304	**A tool is required. Manual mutation does not count.**
305	
306	| Stack | Tool |
307	|---|---|
308	| **TypeScript/JavaScript with Jest (Medusa)** | **StrykerJS with the Jest runner** |
309	| TypeScript/JavaScript with Vitest | StrykerJS with the Vitest runner |
310	| Go | Gremlins or go-mutesting |
311	
312	**Note for us:** Medusa is mixed. Backend packages use **Jest**, the dashboard uses **Vitest**.
313	Pick the runner that matches the files the PR changed.
314	
315	**Set it up early.** Getting the tool to work on a large codebase is real work: builds, services,
316	choosing which tests run. Each student configures and runs the tool for their own files and commits
317	the configuration used. **You may reuse a teammate's setup (and are encouraged to)**, as long as you
318	run the tool yourself and credit the teammate in your report.
319	
320	**Common problems to watch for:**
321	- **The tool stops before mutating.** Tools first run your tests on the unchanged code. If any
322	  selected test fails, the run stops. Fix or exclude failing tests first (this is where the baseline
323	  run helps). *Relevant to us: see HANDOFF section 3 and issue #98.*
324	- **Tests run against built code.** If tests run against compiled output (a `dist` folder) instead
325	  of the source, mutants in the source are never seen. Configure the tool to rebuild before testing,
326	  or choose tests that run on source. *Relevant to us: the integration tests load `dist`.*
327	- **Tests need services.** Some suites need a database or another service running. Start them first.
328	- **False survivors.** If you limit which tests run, make sure the tests that cover the mutated
329	  files are included. Otherwise mutants some test would catch are reported as survived or not
330	  covered. Before writing a new test for a survivor, check that the relevant tests actually ran.
331	- **Long runs.** Mutating only the files changed by the PR keeps run time manageable.
332	
333	**If you are blocked:** ask teammates first, someone may have a working setup. Still stuck, tell the
334	TA **as early as possible**, with the errors and the AI log of what you tried. The TA may approve
335	running the tool on a different issue or part of the code. **Problems reported at the end of the
336	sprint will not excuse a missing D6.**
337	
338	**Submission:** `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-angrapsas.md`, using this template:
339	
340	```markdown
341	# Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <issue title>
342	
343	**PR(s):** #...
344	**Tool:** ...
345	**Config:** [link; credit the teammate if you reused their setup]
346	**Command:** `...`
347	**Reports:** [before](reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json) · [after](reports/<issue#>-<username>-after.json)
348	**Mutation score:** before ...% → after ...%
349	
350	## Surviving mutants
351	
352	| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
353	|---|---|---|---|
354	| | | | |
355	
356	## New or strengthened test
357	
358	Commit: [link] · Test: [file > test name] · Kills: [mutant location]
359	
360	## Questions
361	
362	1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?
363	2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the
364	   requirements? Explain.
365	3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and
366	   what did you verify or correct? If AI was not used, write "N/A."
367	```
368	
369	**Rubric:**
370	
371	| Criterion | Points |
372	|---|---|
373	| Tool run on the files changed by the PR; configuration, command, results and reports committed | 4 |
374	| Surviving mutants analyzed correctly (equivalent vs test gap, with explanation) | 4 |
375	| At least one new or strengthened test kills a surviving mutant; re-run confirms it | 4 |
376	| Answers to the questions show understanding, not just description | 3 |
377	
378	**CSCI 535: the D6 score is the average of the two submissions.**

433	## Grading
434	
435	100 points, 12% of the course grade. D1, D8 and D9 are team; everything else individual.
436	
437	| Deliverable | Points | Notes |
438	|---|---|---|
439	| D1 Sprint Backlog | 10 | Team. Issues selected, scoped with justification, assigned, milestone created; carryover decisions documented |
440	| D2 Requirements Specification | 20 | Individual. User story format, INVEST, AC quality; **spec review on the issue before coding, showing what was checked** |
441	| D3 Design Decisions | 5 | Individual. At least one non-trivial decision per issue, with alternatives |
442	| D4 Pull Requests | 20 | Individual. See detail below |
443	| D5 AI Logs | 5 | Individual. Real logs, correctly named, linked from the issue or PR |
444	| D6 Mutation Testing | 15 | Individual. See rubric above |
445	| D7 Mid-Sprint Check-in | 5 | Individual. On time, substantive, PR linked = 5; late, thin, or no PR = 3; missing = 0 |
446	| D8 Sprint Report | 10 | Team. Completeness, specificity, quality of evidence; suite health section |
447	| D9 Sprint Release | 2 | Team. Tag convention; created after the last merge; description summarizes changes |
448	| D10 Reflection Survey | 8 | Individual. Required for completion |
449	
450	### D4 PR grading detail
451	
452	Aggregate across all PRs, normalized to 20 points.
453	
454	| Criterion | Points per PR |
455	|---|---|
456	| Change correctly implements the acceptance criteria from D2 | 6 |
457	| Tests written or updated appropriately; **Test Evidence section complete**, every AC covered, expected values justified | 6 |
458	| PR description explains what changed and why; **Tech Debt section** present; issue linked | 3 |
459	| CI passes (or manual verification documented) | 3 |
460	| Code reviewed using the rubric (including the test evidence line); reviewer comment posted; **PR merged only after an approval on the latest commit** | 2 |
461	
462	### Minimum bar
463	
464	A team with no merged PRs (D4), no sprint report (D8), or no release (D9) receives a **0** for
465	Sprint 3 regardless of other deliverables.
466	
467	### Extra credit
468	
469	- A PR submitted to the **real upstream project** and accepted or under active review: up to **3
470	  bonus points per PR**, at the instructor's discretion.
471	- A **bug report filed upstream** that comes from your own testing work and is confirmed by the
472	  maintainers (by the time Sprint 4 is graded): up to **2 bonus points per report**.
473	
474	*Note: our Sprint 1 and 2 work produced several real upstream findings (the icons React 19 version

```text
title:	Add Selective Product Duplication Options
state:	OPEN
author:	lefecko
labels:	
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	Team Perseus's Kanban Project (Backlog)
milestone:	
issue-type:	
parent:	
sub-issues:	
sub-issues-completed:	
blocked-by:	
blocking:	
number:	103
--
## User Story
As a store owner, I want to choose which product attributes are copied when duplicating a product so that I can quickly create similar products without having to manually remove or modify unnecessary information.

## User Scenario
Currently, duplicating a product copies a predefined set of its attributes without allowing the store owner to choose what gets included.

A store owner wants to create a new shirt based on an existing product but only wants to copy its basic information, images, and variants, not its prices or inventory quantities.

When the store owner selects the duplicate product action, a modal appears with checkboxes for optional attributes, including images, variants, prices, and inventory settings. Basic product information is always copied.

By default, images, variants, and prices are selected, while inventory quantities are excluded. Inventory settings, such as `manage_inventory` and `allow_backorder`, can be copied separately from actual stock quantities.

The store owner selects the desired attributes and confirms the duplication. The existing backend duplication workflow is modified to respect these selections, creating a new product containing only the requested information.

The duplicated product is always created as a draft to prevent accidental publication. After successful duplication, the store owner is redirected to the new product's details page, where they can review and edit it before publishing.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Selecting the duplicate product action opens a modal allowing the store owner to configure which attributes will be copied.
2. The modal provides checkboxes for images, variants, prices, and inventory settings. Basic product information is always included.
3. Images, variants, and prices are selected by default, while inventory quantities are never copied.
4. Inventory settings (`manage_inventory`, `allow_backorder`, etc.) are treated separately from inventory quantities, allowing settings to be copied without copying stock levels.
5. The existing duplicate product API endpoint accepts the selected duplication options.
6. The backend duplication workflow copies only the selected attributes, while ensuring the duplicated product remains valid.
7. Duplicated products receive new IDs, are always created as drafts, and do not modify the original product.
8. The duplication process handles dependencies between attributes, such as prices requiring corresponding variants.
9. Successful duplication redirects the store owner to the new product's details page. Failed duplication displays an error without redirecting.
10. Automated tests cover different combinations of duplication options, attribute dependencies, draft status, and duplication failures.

## Out of Scope
- Duplicating multiple products simultaneously.
- Changing the original product during duplication.
- Allowing individual variants or images to be selected.
- Copying inventory quantities from the original product.
- Redesigning the product creation or editing forms.
- Adding new product attributes or functionality unrelated to duplication.

## Open Questions
- Should deselecting variants automatically disable prices and inventory settings, or should these options remain visible but unavailable?
- Should the selected duplication options persist between duplication attempts, or reset to the defaults each time?
```

```text
253	/**
254	 * This workflow duplicates a product, including its options, variants, prices
255	 * and relations. It's used by the Duplicate Product Admin API Route.
256	 *
257	 * Unique variant fields (SKU, barcode, EAN, UPC) are left empty on the copy,
258	 * the copy always starts as a draft, and stock levels are not copied: variants
259	 * that manage inventory get new inventory items without stock, created by
260	 * `createProductsWorkflow`.
261	 *
262	 * @example
263	 * const { result } = await duplicateProductWorkflow(container)
264	 * .run({
265	 *   input: {
266	 *     id: "prod_123",
267	 *     title: "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve",
268	 *     handle: "classic-tee-long-sleeve",
269	 *   }
270	 * })
271	 *
272	 * @summary
273	 *
274	 * Duplicate a product with its options, variants and prices.
275	 */
276	export const duplicateProductWorkflow = createWorkflow(
277	  duplicateProductWorkflowId,
278	  (input: WorkflowData<DuplicateProductWorkflowInput>) => {
279	    const { data: source } = useQueryGraphStep({
280	      entity: "product",
281	      fields: DUPLICATE_PRODUCT_FIELDS,
282	      filters: { id: input.id },
283	    }).config({ name: "get-product-to-duplicate" })
284	
285	    const { data: handleConflicts } = useQueryGraphStep({
286	      entity: "product",
287	      fields: ["id"],
288	      filters: { handle: input.handle },
289	    }).config({ name: "get-products-with-handle" })
290	
291	    validateDuplicateProductStep({
292	      source,
293	      handleConflicts,
294	      handle: input.handle,
295	    })
296	
297	    const products = transform({ source, input }, (data) => [
298	      buildDuplicateProductInput({
299	        source: data.source[0],
300	        title: data.input.title,
301	        handle: data.input.handle,
302	      }),
303	    ])
304	
305	    const created = createProductsWorkflow.runAsStep({
306	      input: {
307	        products,
308	        additional_data: input.additional_data,
309	      },
310	    })
311	
312	    return new WorkflowResponse(created)
313	  }
314	)
```

```text
3	  CreatePromotionDTO,
4	  CreatePromotionRuleDTO,
5	} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
6	import { MedusaError, PromotionStatus } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
7	import {
8	  WorkflowData,
9	  WorkflowResponse,
10	  createStep,
11	  createWorkflow,
12	  transform,
13	} from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
14	import { useQueryGraphStep } from "../../common"
15	import { createPromotionsWorkflow } from "./create-promotions"
16	
17	/**
18	 * The fields read from the original promotion, including its rules and their
19	 * values.
20	 */
21	const DUPLICATE_PROMOTION_FIELDS = [
22	  "id",
23	  "type",
24	  "is_automatic",
25	  "is_tax_inclusive",
26	  "limit",
27	  "metadata",
28	  "rules.description",
29	  "rules.attribute",
30	  "rules.operator",
31	  "rules.values.value",
32	  "application_method.type",
33	  "application_method.target_type",
34	  "application_method.allocation",
35	  "application_method.value",
36	  "application_method.currency_code",
37	  "application_method.max_quantity",
38	  "application_method.apply_to_quantity",
39	  "application_method.buy_rules_min_quantity",
40	  "application_method.target_rules.description",
41	  "application_method.target_rules.attribute",
42	  "application_method.target_rules.operator",
43	  "application_method.target_rules.values.value",
44	  "application_method.buy_rules.description",
45	  "application_method.buy_rules.attribute",
46	  "application_method.buy_rules.operator",
47	  "application_method.buy_rules.values.value",
48	]
49	
50	/**
51	 * The data to duplicate a promotion, along with custom data that's passed to
52	 * the hooks of the underlying create workflow.
53	 */
54	export type DuplicatePromotionWorkflowInput = {
55	  /**
56	   * The ID of the promotion to duplicate.
57	   */
58	  id: string
59	  /**
60	   * The code of the new promotion. It must not be used by another promotion.
61	   */
62	  code: string
63	} & AdditionalData
64	
65	/**
66	 * The data to validate before duplicating a promotion.
67	 */
68	export interface ValidateDuplicatePromotionStepInput {
69	  /**
70	   * The promotions matching the requested ID (empty if it does not exist).
71	   */
72	  source: { id: string }[]
73	  /**
74	   * The promotions already using the requested code.
75	   */
76	  codeConflicts: { id: string }[]
77	  /**
78	   * The requested code for the copy.
79	   */
80	  code: string
81	}
82	
83	export const validateDuplicatePromotionStepId = "validate-duplicate-promotion"
84	/**
85	 * This step validates a duplicate request. It throws if the original promotion
86	 * is missing or if the code is already used by another promotion, before
87	 * anything is created.
88	 */
89	export const validateDuplicatePromotionStep = createStep(
90	  validateDuplicatePromotionStepId,
91	  async (data: ValidateDuplicatePromotionStepInput) => {
92	    if (!data.source[0]) {
93	      throw new MedusaError(
94	        MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
95	        "Promotion to duplicate was not found"
96	      )
97	    }
98	
99	    // Same message as the create API gives for a code that's taken.
100	    if (data.codeConflicts.length) {
101	      throw new MedusaError(
102	        MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
103	        `Promotion with code: ${data.code}, already exists.`
104	      )
105	    }
106	  }
107	)
108	
109	/**
110	 * Copies rules as new rules, so the copy doesn't share rule rows with the
111	 * original.
112	 */
113	const copyRules = (rules?: Record<string, any>[]): CreatePromotionRuleDTO[] =>
114	  (rules ?? []).map((rule) => ({
115	    description: rule.description,
116	    attribute: rule.attribute,
117	    operator: rule.operator,
118	    values: rule.values.map((value: { value: string }) => value.value),
119	  }))
120	
121	/**
122	 * Maps a loaded promotion to the input of `createPromotionsWorkflow`. The copy
123	 * always starts as a draft with no usage, and it isn't added to the original's
124	 * campaign.
125	 */
126	export const buildDuplicatePromotionInput = (
127	  source: Record<string, any>,
128	  code: string
129	): CreatePromotionDTO => {
130	  const method = source.application_method
131	
132	  return {
133	    code,
134	    type: source.type,
135	    status: PromotionStatus.DRAFT,
136	    is_automatic: source.is_automatic,
137	    is_tax_inclusive: source.is_tax_inclusive,
138	    limit: source.limit,
139	    metadata: source.metadata,
140	    rules: copyRules(source.rules),
141	    application_method: {
142	      type: method.type,
143	      target_type: method.target_type,
144	      allocation: method.allocation,
145	      value: method.value,
146	      currency_code: method.currency_code,
147	      max_quantity: method.max_quantity,
148	      apply_to_quantity: method.apply_to_quantity,
149	      buy_rules_min_quantity: method.buy_rules_min_quantity,
150	      target_rules: copyRules(method.target_rules),
151	      buy_rules: copyRules(method.buy_rules),
152	    },
153	  }
154	}
155	
156	export const duplicatePromotionWorkflowId = "duplicate-promotion"
157	/**
158	 * This workflow duplicates a promotion, including its conditions, target rules
159	 * and buy rules. It's used by the Duplicate Promotion Admin API Route.
160	 *
161	 * The copy always starts as a draft with a usage count of 0, its rules are new
162	 * rules rather than shared with the original, and it isn't added to the
163	 * original's campaign.
164	 *
165	 * @example
166	 * const { result } = await duplicatePromotionWorkflow(container)
167	 * .run({
168	 *   input: {
169	 *     id: "promo_123",
170	 *     code: "FALL20",
171	 *   }
172	 * })
173	 *
174	 * @summary
175	 *
176	 * Duplicate a promotion with its rules.
177	 */
178	export const duplicatePromotionWorkflow = createWorkflow(
179	  duplicatePromotionWorkflowId,
180	  (input: WorkflowData<DuplicatePromotionWorkflowInput>) => {
181	    const { data: source } = useQueryGraphStep({
182	      entity: "promotion",
183	      fields: DUPLICATE_PROMOTION_FIELDS,
184	      filters: { id: input.id },
185	    }).config({ name: "get-promotion-to-duplicate" })
186	
187	    const { data: codeConflicts } = useQueryGraphStep({
188	      entity: "promotion",
189	      fields: ["id"],
190	      filters: { code: input.code },
191	    }).config({ name: "get-promotions-with-code" })
192	
193	    validateDuplicatePromotionStep({
194	      source,
195	      codeConflicts,
196	      code: input.code,
197	    })
198	
199	    const promotionsData = transform({ source, input }, (data) => [
200	      buildDuplicatePromotionInput(data.source[0], data.input.code),
201	    ])
202	
203	    const created = createPromotionsWorkflow.runAsStep({
204	      input: {
205	        promotionsData,
206	        additional_data: input.additional_data,
207	      },
208	    })
209	
210	    return new WorkflowResponse(created)
211	  }
212	)
213
```

```text
18	/**

24	 * `@hookform/resolvers` (3.4.2) cannot catch zod 4 validation errors: it
25	 * rethrows them, so an empty field would never show an error.

27	const resolver: Resolver<DuplicateProductValues> = async (values) => {
28	  const title = values.title.trim()
29	  const handle = values.handle.trim()
30	  const errors: FieldErrors<DuplicateProductValues> = {}
31	
32	  if (!title) {
33	    errors.title = { type: "required", message: "" }
34	  }
35	
36	  if (!handle) {
37	    errors.handle = { type: "required", message: "" }
38	  }
39	
40	  return Object.keys(errors).length
41	    ? { values: {}, errors }
42	    : { values: { title, handle }, errors: {} }
43	}
```

```text
    describe("POST /admin/products/:id/duplicate", () => {
      it("duplicates a product with its structure and clears unique fields", async () => {
        const response = await api.post(
          `/admin/products/${original.id}/duplicate?fields=${FIELDS}`,
          { title: "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve", handle: "classic-tee-ls" },
          adminHeaders
        )

        expect(response.status).toEqual(200)

        const copy = response.data.product

        expect(copy.id).not.toEqual(original.id)
        expect(copy).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            title: "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve",
            handle: "classic-tee-ls",
            // Always a draft, even though the original is published.
            status: "draft",
            subtitle: "Cotton",
            description: "A classic tee",
            discountable: false,
            metadata: { season: "summer" },
            thumbnail: "https://example.com/thumb.png",
          })
        )
        expect(copy.images.map((i) => i.url)).toEqual([
          "https://example.com/1.png",
        ])
        expect(copy.tags.map((t) => t.id)).toEqual([tag.id])
        expect(copy.shipping_profile.id).toEqual(shippingProfile.id)

        // Options and values are copied.
        expect(
          copy.options.map((o) => ({
            title: o.title,
            values: o.values.map((v) => v.value).sort(),
          }))
        ).toEqual(
          expect.arrayContaining([
            { title: "Color", values: ["Blue", "Red"] },
            { title: "Size", values: ["M", "S"] },
          ])
        )

        // Variants, option values and prices are copied.
        expect(copy.variants).toHaveLength(2)
        const redSmall = copy.variants.find((v) => v.title === "Red / S")
        expect(redSmall.manage_inventory).toEqual(true)
        expect(redSmall.metadata).toEqual({ fit: "slim" })
        expect(redSmall.options.map((o) => o.value).sort()).toEqual([
          "Red",
          "S",
        ])
        expect(
          redSmall.prices.map((p) => [p.currency_code, p.amount]).sort()
        ).toEqual([
          ["eur", 9],
          ["usd", 10],
        ])

        // Unique fields are left empty.
        for (const variant of copy.variants) {
          expect(variant.sku).toBeNull()
          expect(variant.barcode).toBeNull()
          expect(variant.ean).toBeNull()
          expect(variant.upc).toBeNull()
        }

        // Variants and options belong to the copy, not the original.
        const originalAfter = (
          await api.get(
            `/admin/products/${original.id}?fields=${FIELDS}`,
            adminHeaders
          )
        ).data.product
        const originalVariantIds = originalAfter.variants.map((v) => v.id)
        for (const variant of copy.variants) {
          expect(originalVariantIds).not.toContain(variant.id)
        }
      })

      it("leaves the original product unchanged", async () => {
        await api.post(
          `/admin/products/${original.id}/duplicate`,
          { title: "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve", handle: "classic-tee-ls" },
          adminHeaders
        )

        const after = (
          await api.get(
            `/admin/products/${original.id}?fields=${FIELDS}`,
            adminHeaders
          )
        ).data.product

        expect(after.title).toEqual("Classic Tee")
        expect(after.handle).toEqual("classic-tee")
        expect(after.status).toEqual("published")
        expect(after.variants.map((v) => v.sku).sort()).toEqual([
          "TEE-BLUE-M",
          "TEE-RED-S",
        ])
      })

      it("creates new inventory items without stock for managed variants", async () => {
        const { product: copy } = (
          await api.post(
            `/admin/products/${original.id}/duplicate?fields=*variants`,
            { title: "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve", handle: "classic-tee-ls" },
            adminHeaders
          )
        ).data

        const managed = copy.variants.find((v) => v.title === "Red / S")

        const { data } = await api.get(
          `/admin/products/${copy.id}/variants/${managed.id}?fields=*inventory_items,*inventory_items.inventory,*inventory_items.inventory.location_levels`,
          adminHeaders
        )

        const items = data.variant.inventory_items ?? []
        expect(items).toHaveLength(1)
        // No stock is copied: the new item has no stocked locations.
        expect(items[0].inventory.location_levels ?? []).toHaveLength(0)
      })

      it("fails when the handle is already used and creates nothing", async () => {
        const before = (await api.get("/admin/products", adminHeaders)).data
          .count

        const error = await api
          .post(
            `/admin/products/${original.id}/duplicate`,
            { title: "Another Tee", handle: "classic-tee" },
            adminHeaders
          )
          .catch((e) => e)

        expect(error.response.status).toEqual(400)
        expect(error.response.data.message).toContain("already exists")

        const after = (await api.get("/admin/products", adminHeaders)).data
          .count
        expect(after).toEqual(before)
      })

      it("accepts the pre-filled '(Copy)' title and handle as they are", async () => {
        // No rename is required: the dashboard pre-fills these values and
        // the owner may keep them.
        const response = await api.post(
          `/admin/products/${original.id}/duplicate`,
          { title: "Classic Tee (Copy)", handle: "classic-tee-copy" },
          adminHeaders
        )

        expect(response.status).toEqual(200)
        expect(response.data.product).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            title: "Classic Tee (Copy)",
            handle: "classic-tee-copy",
            status: "draft",
          })
        )
      })

      it("rejects an empty title", async () => {
        const before = (await api.get("/admin/products", adminHeaders)).data
          .count

        const error = await api
          .post(
            `/admin/products/${original.id}/duplicate`,
            { title: "", handle: "classic-tee-new" },
            adminHeaders
          )
          .catch((e) => e)

        expect(error.response.status).toEqual(400)

        const after = (await api.get("/admin/products", adminHeaders)).data
          .count
        expect(after).toEqual(before)
      })

      it("returns 404 for an unknown product", async () => {
        const error = await api
          .post(
            `/admin/products/prod_missing/duplicate`,
            { title: "Whatever", handle: "whatever" },
            adminHeaders
          )
          .catch((e) => e)

        expect(error.response.status).toEqual(404)
      })
    })
  },
})
```

```text
        const productsData = data.input.products.map((p) => {
```

```text
export const validateProductInputStep = createStep(
  validateProductInputStepId,
  async (data: ValidateProductInputStepInput) => {
    const { products } = data

    const missingOptionsProductTitles = products
      .filter((product) => !product.options?.length)
      .map((product) => product.title)

    if (missingOptionsProductTitles.length) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
        `Product options are not provided for: [${missingOptionsProductTitles.join(
          ", "
        )}].`
      )
    }
  }
)
```

Worktree is up at `~/medusa-103` on `feat/issue-103-selective-duplication`. I've read #103 and the existing code. Nothing written or posted yet.

## Verdict: yes, genuinely small, but at the top of the range

The plumbing all exists. lefecko's #82 (duplicate product) and my #63 (duplicate promotion) already built the route, the workflow, the drawer form, the SDK method and the i18n block. #103 does not add a feature path, it threads an options object through one pure function and adds checkboxes to a form that already exists. Core code delta is roughly 80 to 100 lines.

**What's already true today**, so 3 of the 10 ACs are regression-only:
- AC3's "inventory quantities are never copied" — `duplicate-product.ts:258-261`, managed variants get fresh inventory items with no stock. There's an integration test for it already.
- AC7 (new IDs, always draft, original untouched) — `buildDuplicateProductInput` hardcodes `status: "draft"` at line 180, and there are two integration tests covering it.
- AC9 (redirect on success, error toast with no redirect) — `duplicate-product-form.tsx:66-76`, covered by the existing vitest spec.

**What's actually new:**

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `core-flows/.../duplicate-product.ts` | options type + branches in `buildDuplicateProductInput` |
| `medusa/src/api/admin/products/validators.ts:296` | extend the `DuplicateProduct` zod object |
| `.../products/[id]/duplicate/route.ts` | pass the options through |
| `core/types/.../product/admin/payloads.ts:454` | extend `AdminDuplicateProduct` |
| `js-sdk/src/admin/product.ts:350` | TSDoc only |
| `.../duplicate-product-form.tsx` | 4 checkboxes + the dependency disable logic |
| `i18n/translations/en.json` | labels under `products.duplicate` |

Plus a new unit spec, additions to `integration-tests/http/__tests__/product/admin/product-duplicate.spec.ts`, additions to the form spec, and a changeset.

## One hard constraint the issue doesn't account for

`createProductsWorkflow` **throws if `options` is empty** (`create-products.ts:79-88`, `"Product options are not provided for: [...]"`). So options can never be optional. Unchecking variants has to still copy the options and produce a product with options and zero variants. AC2 only says "basic product information is always included", which doesn't cover options, and AC8 ("handles dependencies between attributes") points the opposite way. The spec needs to say this explicitly or the implementation will contradict it.

## Four things to settle before coding

The issue asks two of these itself, which means the spec is incomplete as written and D2 is graded on exactly that:

1. Deselecting variants: disable prices and inventory settings, or leave them visible but inert? (the issue's own Q1)
2. Do selections persist between attempts or reset to defaults? (the issue's own Q2)
3. **The one that can silently ship wrong behavior:** what does "inventory settings not copied" mean? Omitting them falls through to the model defaults, `manage_inventory: true` and `allow_backorder: false` (`product-variant.ts:13-14`). So "not copied" still gives you a managed variant. If the intent is an unmanaged variant, the code has to send `manage_inventory: false` explicitly. AC4 doesn't say.
4. AC10 says tests cover "different combinations" of 4 booleans. 16 combos is not worth writing. I'd commit the spec to a named set of about 6 cases so the reviewer and I agree on what "covers combinations" means.

## Bonus worth knowing

There is **no unit test anywhere** for `buildDuplicateProductInput` or `buildDuplicatePromotionInput` (confirmed by grep across the repo). After this change it becomes a pure function with a dozen branches and zero existing coverage, which is close to an ideal StrykerJS target for one of your two D6 submissions, on a file your own PR changed.

One scope-label note: #103 currently has **no labels and no milestone**, and `sprint3.md` lists its scope as blank. D1 requires a stated scope with justification, so lefecko needs to add "small" with a sentence, or I ask for it when I claim.

Next step per your instructions is to claim the issue and request a spec review. Before I draft either, how do you want to handle the four open questions? I'd rather put my proposed answers in the claim comment and have lefecko confirm or push back as part of the spec review, instead of asking cold and waiting on a round trip. Tell me if you'd rather ask them open-ended.

```text
"use client"

import { CheckMini, MinusMini } from "@medusajs/icons"
import { Checkbox as RadixCheckbox } from "radix-ui"
import * as React from "react"

import { clx } from "@/utils/clx"
import { CheckboxCheckedState } from "./types"

/**
 * This component is based on the [Radix UI Checkbox](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/checkbox) primitive.
 */
const Checkbox = React.forwardRef<
  React.ElementRef<typeof RadixCheckbox.Root>,
  React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof RadixCheckbox.Root> & {
    checked?: CheckboxCheckedState | undefined
  }
>(({ className, checked, ...props }, ref) => {
  return (
    <RadixCheckbox.Root
      {...props}
      ref={ref}
      checked={checked}
      className={clx(
        "group inline-flex h-5 w-5 items-center justify-center outline-none ",
        className
      )}
    >
      <div
        className={clx(
          "text-ui-fg-on-inverted bg-ui-bg-base shadow-borders-base [&_path]:shadow-details-contrast-on-bg-interactive transition-fg h-[15px] w-[15px] rounded-[3px]",
          "group-disabled:cursor-not-allowed group-disabled:opacity-50",
          "group-focus-visible:!shadow-borders-interactive-with-focus",
          "group-hover:group-enabled:group-data-[state=unchecked]:bg-ui-bg-base-hover",
          "group-data-[state=checked]:bg-ui-bg-interactive group-data-[state=checked]:shadow-borders-interactive-with-shadow",
          "group-data-[state=indeterminate]:bg-ui-bg-interactive group-data-[state=indeterminate]:shadow-borders-interactive-with-shadow"
        )}
      >
        <RadixCheckbox.Indicator>
          {checked === "indeterminate" ? <MinusMini /> : <CheckMini />}
        </RadixCheckbox.Indicator>
      </div>
    </RadixCheckbox.Root>
  )
})
Checkbox.displayName = "Checkbox"

export { Checkbox }
```

```bash
mkdir -p ~/medusa-103/packages/core/core-flows/src/product/workflows/__tests__ && cat > ~/medusa-103/packages/core/core-flows/src/product/workflows/__tests__/duplicate-product.spec.ts <<'EOF'
import {
  buildDuplicateProductInput,
  resolveDuplicateProductInclude,
} from "../duplicate-product"

// A source product shaped the way `DUPLICATE_PRODUCT_FIELDS` loads it: one
// option with two values, one managed variant with two prices, one image.
const source = (overrides: Record<string, unknown> = {}): any => ({
  id: "prod_1",
  title: "Classic Tee",
  handle: "classic-tee",
  subtitle: "Cotton",
  description: "A classic tee",
  is_giftcard: false,
  discountable: false,
  thumbnail: "https://example.com/thumb.png",
  weight: 100,
  metadata: { season: "summer" },
  type_id: "ptyp_1",
  collection_id: "pcol_1",
  images: [{ url: "https://example.com/1.png", metadata: { alt: "front" } }],
  options: [{ title: "Size", values: [{ value: "S" }, { value: "M" }] }],
  tags: [{ id: "ptag_1" }],
  categories: [{ id: "pcat_1" }],
  sales_channels: [{ id: "sc_1" }],
  shipping_profile: { id: "sp_1" },
  variants: [
    {
      title: "S",
      manage_inventory: false,
      allow_backorder: true,
      variant_rank: 0,
      weight: 90,
      metadata: { fit: "slim" },
      options: [{ value: "S", option: { title: "Size" } }],
      prices: [
        {
          amount: 10,
          currency_code: "usd",
          min_quantity: 1,
          max_quantity: 5,
          price_rules: [{ attribute: "region_id", value: "reg_1" }],
        },
        { amount: 9, currency_code: "eur", price_rules: [] },
      ],
    },
  ],
  ...overrides,
})

const build = (include?: any, overrides: Record<string, unknown> = {}) =>
  buildDuplicateProductInput({
    source: source(overrides),
    title: "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve",
    handle: "classic-tee-ls",
    include: resolveDuplicateProductInclude(include),
  })

describe("resolveDuplicateProductInclude", () => {
  // AC3: the defaults keep the behaviour duplication had before the options
  // existed, so an unchanged request copies everything it used to.
  it("selects every group when nothing is requested", () => {
    expect(resolveDuplicateProductInclude()).toEqual({
      images: true,
      variants: true,
      prices: true,
      inventory_settings: true,
    })
  })

  it("selects every group for an empty selection", () => {
    expect(resolveDuplicateProductInclude({})).toEqual({
      images: true,
      variants: true,
      prices: true,
      inventory_settings: true,
    })
  })

  it("keeps the groups that are not mentioned", () => {
    expect(resolveDuplicateProductInclude({ images: false })).toEqual({
      images: false,
      variants: true,
      prices: true,
      inventory_settings: true,
    })
  })

  // AC8: prices and inventory settings are stored on variants, so they cannot
  // be copied on their own.
  it("forces prices and inventory settings off when variants are off", () => {
    expect(
      resolveDuplicateProductInclude({
        variants: false,
        prices: true,
        inventory_settings: true,
      })
    ).toEqual({
      images: true,
      variants: false,
      prices: false,
      inventory_settings: false,
    })
  })

  it("keeps prices off when variants are on but prices are not wanted", () => {
    expect(
      resolveDuplicateProductInclude({ variants: true, prices: false })
    ).toEqual({
      images: true,
      variants: true,
      prices: false,
      inventory_settings: true,
    })
  })
})

describe("buildDuplicateProductInput", () => {
  describe("always copied, whatever is selected", () => {
    // AC2: basic product information is not optional.
    it("copies the basic fields and the requested title and handle", () => {
      const result: any = build({
        images: false,
        variants: false,
        prices: false,
        inventory_settings: false,
      })

      expect(result).toEqual(
        expect.objectContaining({
          title: "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve",
          handle: "classic-tee-ls",
          subtitle: "Cotton",
          description: "A classic tee",
          is_giftcard: false,
          discountable: false,
          weight: 100,
          metadata: { season: "summer" },
          type_id: "ptyp_1",
          collection_id: "pcol_1",
          tag_ids: ["ptag_1"],
          category_ids: ["pcat_1"],
          sales_channels: [{ id: "sc_1" }],
          shipping_profile_id: "sp_1",
        })
      )
    })

    // AC7: the copy is a draft whatever the original's status is.
    it("always starts the copy as a draft", () => {
      expect(build({}).status).toEqual("draft")
      expect(build({ variants: false }).status).toEqual("draft")
      expect(
        build({}, { status: "published" }).status
      ).toEqual("draft")
    })

    // The create workflow rejects a product with no options, so options are
    // copied even when the variants that use them are not.
    it("copies options even when variants are not copied", () => {
      const result: any = build({ variants: false })

      expect(result.options).toEqual([{ title: "Size", values: ["S", "M"] }])
    })

    it("trims the requested title", () => {
      const result = buildDuplicateProductInput({
        source: source(),
        title: "  Padded Title  ",
        handle: "padded-title",
        include: resolveDuplicateProductInclude(),
      })

      expect(result.title).toEqual("Padded Title")
    })
  })

  describe("images", () => {
    it("copies image urls and metadata when selected", () => {
      const result: any = build({ images: true })

      expect(result.images).toEqual([
        { url: "https://example.com/1.png", metadata: { alt: "front" } },
      ])
    })

    it("copies no images when not selected", () => {
      const result: any = build({ images: false })

      expect(result.images).toEqual([])
    })

    it("copies no images when the original has none", () => {
      const result: any = build({ images: true }, { images: [] })

      expect(result.images).toEqual([])
    })
  })

  describe("variants", () => {
    it("copies variants with their option values when selected", () => {
      const result: any = build({ variants: true })

      expect(result.variants).toHaveLength(1)
      expect(result.variants[0]).toEqual(
        expect.objectContaining({
          title: "S",
          variant_rank: 0,
          weight: 90,
          metadata: { fit: "slim" },
          options: { Size: "S" },
        })
      )
    })

    it("copies no variants when not selected", () => {
      const result: any = build({ variants: false })

      expect(result.variants).toEqual([])
    })

    // Unique columns stay empty so the copy does not collide with the original.
    it("never copies sku, barcode, ean or upc", () => {
      const result: any = build(
        {},
        {
          variants: [
            {
              title: "S",
              sku: "TEE-S",
              barcode: "123",
              ean: "456",
              upc: "789",
              options: [],
              prices: [],
            },
          ],
        }
      )

      expect(result.variants[0]).not.toHaveProperty("sku")
      expect(result.variants[0]).not.toHaveProperty("barcode")
      expect(result.variants[0]).not.toHaveProperty("ean")
      expect(result.variants[0]).not.toHaveProperty("upc")
    })
  })

  describe("prices", () => {
    it("copies every price with its rules when selected", () => {
      const result: any = build({ prices: true })

      expect(result.variants[0].prices).toEqual([
        {
          amount: 10,
          currency_code: "usd",
          min_quantity: 1,
          max_quantity: 5,
          rules: { region_id: "reg_1" },
        },
        {
          amount: 9,
          currency_code: "eur",
          min_quantity: undefined,
          max_quantity: undefined,
          rules: {},
        },
      ])
    })

    it("copies the variant without prices when prices are not selected", () => {
      const result: any = build({ prices: false })

      expect(result.variants).toHaveLength(1)
      expect(result.variants[0].prices).toEqual([])
    })
  })

  describe("inventory settings", () => {
    // AC4: the settings are copied from the original when selected.
    it("copies manage_inventory and allow_backorder when selected", () => {
      const result: any = build({ inventory_settings: true })

      expect(result.variants[0].manage_inventory).toEqual(false)
      expect(result.variants[0].allow_backorder).toEqual(true)
    })

    // Omitted rather than set, so the variant falls back to the product
    // module's own defaults (manage_inventory true, allow_backorder false).
    it("omits both fields when not selected", () => {
      const result: any = build({ inventory_settings: false })

      expect(result.variants[0]).not.toHaveProperty("manage_inventory")
      expect(result.variants[0]).not.toHaveProperty("allow_backorder")
    })

    // AC4: settings are independent of stock, which is never part of the input.
    it("never copies stock quantities", () => {
      const result: any = build(
        { inventory_settings: true },
        {
          variants: [
            {
              title: "S",
              manage_inventory: true,
              inventory_quantity: 42,
              options: [],
              prices: [],
            },
          ],
        }
      )

      expect(result.variants[0]).not.toHaveProperty("inventory_quantity")
    })
  })

  describe("combinations", () => {
    // AC6: the narrowest selection still produces a product the create
    // workflow accepts, which means a title, a handle and options.
    it("builds a valid product for the narrowest selection", () => {
      const result: any = build({
        images: false,
        variants: false,
        prices: false,
        inventory_settings: false,
      })

      expect(result.title).toEqual("Classic Tee - Long Sleeve")
      expect(result.handle).toEqual("classic-tee-ls")
      expect(result.options).toHaveLength(1)
      expect(result.images).toEqual([])
      expect(result.variants).toEqual([])
    })

    it("copies variants without prices or inventory settings", () => {
      const result: any = build({
        images: false,
        variants: true,
        prices: false,
        inventory_settings: false,
      })

      expect(result.images).toEqual([])
      expect(result.variants[0].title).toEqual("S")
      expect(result.variants[0].prices).toEqual([])
      expect(result.variants[0]).not.toHaveProperty("manage_inventory")
    })

    it("copies images only", () => {
      const result: any = build({
        images: true,
        variants: false,
        prices: false,
        inventory_settings: false,
      })

      expect(result.images).toHaveLength(1)
      expect(result.variants).toEqual([])
    })

    it("copies prices but not inventory settings", () => {
      const result: any = build({
        prices: true,
        inventory_settings: false,
      })

      expect(result.variants[0].prices).toHaveLength(2)
      expect(result.variants[0]).not.toHaveProperty("manage_inventory")
    })
  })
})
```

```bash
export type DuplicateProductInclude = {

  variants?: boolean
  /**

  /**
   * Whether to copy the variants' `manage_inventory` and `allow_backorder`
   * settings. Stock quantities are never copied. Requires `variants`.

  inventory_settings?: boolean

/**
 * Fills in the groups a request left out and applies the dependencies between
 * them: prices and inventory settings are stored on variants, so neither can
 * be copied when variants are not.
 *
 * Everything defaults to copied, which is what duplication did before the
 * groups existed, so an unchanged request behaves as it always has.
 */
export const resolveDuplicateProductInclude = (
  include?: DuplicateProductInclude
): Required<DuplicateProductInclude> => {
  const variants = include?.variants ?? true

  return {
    images: include?.images ?? true,
    variants,
    prices: variants && (include?.prices ?? true),
    inventory_settings: variants && (include?.inventory_settings ?? true),
  }
}

  include?: DuplicateProductInclude
```

```text
export const validateDuplicateProductStep = createStep(
  validateDuplicateProductStepId,
  async (data: ValidateDuplicateProductStepInput) => {
    const [source] = data.source

    if (!source) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
        "Product to duplicate was not found"
      )
    }

    // Issue #112: a copy would keep the bundle marker in its metadata but not
    // the component inventory links, which would produce a broken bundle.
    // Create a new bundle with the bundle API instead.
    if (isBundleMetadata(source.metadata)) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
        "A bundle can't be duplicated. Create a new bundle instead."
      )
    }

    if (data.handleConflicts.length) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
        `Product with handle "${data.handle}" already exists.`
      )
    }
  }
)

/**
 * The data to build the create payload for the copy.
 */
export interface BuildDuplicateProductInputStepInput {
  /**
   * The fully loaded source product.
   */
  source: Record<string, any>
  /**
   * The title of the copy.

  title: string
  /**

   */
  handle: string
  /**

  include: Required<DuplicateProductInclude>
}

/**
 * Maps a loaded product to the input of `createProductsWorkflow`, copying only
 * the groups `data.include` selects.

 * This is a plain function (used inside `transform`) so it stays easy to
 * unit test. Unique variant fields (sku, barcode, ean, upc) are deliberately
 * never copied, and the copy always starts as a draft.
 */
export const buildDuplicateProductInput = (
  data: BuildDuplicateProductInputStepInput
): CreateProductWorkflowInputDTO => {
  const { source, include } = data

  return {
    title: data.title.trim(),
    handle: data.handle,
    // A copy is never published automatically, whatever the original is.
    status: "draft",
    subtitle: source.subtitle,
    description: source.description,
    is_giftcard: source.is_giftcard,
    discountable: source.discountable,
    thumbnail: source.thumbnail,
    // Images point at the same file URLs as the original.
    images: include.images
      ? (source.images ?? []).map((image: any) => ({
          url: image.url,
          metadata: image.metadata,
        }))
      : [],
    weight: source.weight,
    length: source.length,
    height: source.height,
    width: source.width,
    hs_code: source.hs_code,
    origin_country: source.origin_country,
    mid_code: source.mid_code,
    material: source.material,
    metadata: source.metadata,
    type_id: source.type_id,
    collection_id: source.collection_id,
    tag_ids: (source.tags ?? []).map((tag: any) => tag.id),
    category_ids: (source.categories ?? []).map((category: any) => category.id),
    sales_channels: (source.sales_channels ?? []).map((channel: any) => ({
      id: channel.id,
    })),
    shipping_profile_id: source.shipping_profile?.id,
    // Options are always copied: `createProductsWorkflow` rejects a product
    // that has none, so a copy without variants still needs them.
    options: (source.options ?? []).map((option: any) => ({
      title: option.title,
      values: (option.values ?? []).map((value: any) => value.value),
    })),
    variants: include.variants
      ? (source.variants ?? []).map((variant: any) =>

        )

  } as CreateProductWorkflowInputDTO
}
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Rewrite duplicate product form with checkboxes

```bash
cd ~/medusa-103 && cat > packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/products/product-duplicate/components/duplicate-product-form/duplicate-product-form.tsx <<'EOF'
import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
import { Button, Checkbox, Hint, Input, Text, toast } from "@medusajs/ui"
import { FieldErrors, Resolver, useForm, useWatch } from "react-hook-form"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
import { useNavigate } from "react-router-dom"

import { Form } from "../../../../../components/common/form"
import { RouteDrawer } from "../../../../../components/modals"
import { KeyboundForm } from "../../../../../components/utilities/keybound-form"
import { useDuplicateProduct } from "../../../../../hooks/api/products"

type DuplicateProductFormProps = {
  product: Pick<HttpTypes.AdminProduct, "id" | "title" | "handle">
}

type DuplicateProductInclude = {
  images: boolean
  variants: boolean
  prices: boolean
  inventory_settings: boolean
}

type DuplicateProductValues = {
  title: string
  handle: string
  include: DuplicateProductInclude
}

/**
 * The groups the owner can choose from, in the order they are shown. Prices and
 * inventory settings are stored on the variants, so they are only available
 * when variants are copied.
 */
const INCLUDE_FIELDS: {
  name: keyof DuplicateProductInclude
  labelKey: string
  requiresVariants: boolean
}[] = [
  { name: "images", labelKey: "products.duplicate.include.images", requiresVariants: false },
  { name: "variants", labelKey: "products.duplicate.include.variants", requiresVariants: false },
  { name: "prices", labelKey: "products.duplicate.include.prices", requiresVariants: true },
  {
    name: "inventory_settings",
    labelKey: "products.duplicate.include.inventorySettings",
    requiresVariants: true,
  },
]

/**
 * Both text fields are required, nothing else is checked here. The groups are
 * booleans, and any combination of them is valid. The server still checks that
 * the handle is not already used by another product and the error is shown as
 * a toast.
 *
 * This is a plain resolver instead of `zodResolver` because the installed
 * `@hookform/resolvers` (3.4.2) cannot catch zod 4 validation errors: it
 * rethrows them, so an empty field would never show an error.
 */
const resolver: Resolver<DuplicateProductValues> = async (values) => {
  const title = values.title.trim()
  const handle = values.handle.trim()
  const errors: FieldErrors<DuplicateProductValues> = {}

  if (!title) {
    errors.title = { type: "required", message: "" }
  }

  if (!handle) {
    errors.handle = { type: "required", message: "" }
  }

  return Object.keys(errors).length
    ? { values: {}, errors }
    : { values: { title, handle, include: values.include }, errors: {} }
}

export const DuplicateProductForm = ({
  product,
}: DuplicateProductFormProps) => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()
  const navigate = useNavigate()

  const form = useForm<DuplicateProductValues>({
    // Pre-filled as a starting point; the owner can keep or edit both values.
    // Every group starts selected, so duplicating without touching the
    // checkboxes copies the whole product. The selection is not remembered
    // between attempts.
    defaultValues: {
      title: `${product.title} (Copy)`,
      handle: `${product.handle}-copy`,
      include: {
        images: true,
        variants: true,
        prices: true,
        inventory_settings: true,
      },
    },
    resolver,
  })

  const variantsSelected = useWatch({
    control: form.control,
    name: "include.variants",
  })

  const { mutateAsync, isPending } = useDuplicateProduct(product.id)

  /**
   * Unselecting variants also unselects the two groups that depend on them, so
   * the payload always matches the checkboxes the owner can see.
   */
  const onVariantsChange = (checked: boolean) => {
    form.setValue("include.variants", checked)

    if (!checked) {
      form.setValue("include.prices", false)
      form.setValue("include.inventory_settings", false)
    }
  }

  const handleSubmit = form.handleSubmit(async (data) => {
    await mutateAsync(
      {
        title: data.title.trim(),
        handle: data.handle.trim(),
        include: data.include,
      },
      {
        onSuccess: ({ product: created }) => {
          toast.success(
            t("products.duplicate.successToast", { title: created.title })
          )
          // Land on the new draft product, not the original.
          navigate(`/products/${created.id}`, { replace: true })
        },
        onError: (e) => {
          // e.g. the handle is already used by another product.
          toast.error(e.message)
        },
      }
    )
  })

  return (
    <RouteDrawer.Form form={form}>
      <KeyboundForm
        onSubmit={handleSubmit}
        className="flex flex-1 flex-col overflow-hidden"
      >
        <RouteDrawer.Body className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-y-4 overflow-y-auto">
          <Form.Field
            control={form.control}
            name="title"
            render={({ field }) => {
              return (
                <Form.Item>
                  <Form.Label>{t("fields.title")}</Form.Label>
                  <Form.Control>
                    <Input {...field} />
                  </Form.Control>
                  <Form.ErrorMessage />
                </Form.Item>
              )
            }}
          />
          <Form.Field
            control={form.control}
            name="handle"
            render={({ field }) => {
              return (
                <Form.Item>
                  <Form.Label>{t("fields.handle")}</Form.Label>
                  <Form.Control>
                    <Input {...field} />
                  </Form.Control>
                  <Form.ErrorMessage />
                </Form.Item>
              )
            }}
          />
          <div className="flex flex-col gap-y-3">
            <Text size="small" weight="plus" leading="compact">
              {t("products.duplicate.include.label")}
            </Text>
            {INCLUDE_FIELDS.map(({ name, labelKey, requiresVariants }) => {
              const disabled = requiresVariants && !variantsSelected

              return (
                <Form.Field
                  key={name}
                  control={form.control}
                  name={`include.${name}`}
                  render={({ field: { value, onChange, ...field } }) => {
                    return (
                      <Form.Item>
                        <div className="flex items-center gap-x-2">
                          <Form.Control>
                            <Checkbox
                              {...field}
                              checked={value}
                              disabled={disabled}
                              onCheckedChange={(checked) =>
                                name === "variants"
                                  ? onVariantsChange(!!checked)
                                  : onChange(!!checked)
                              }
                            />
                          </Form.Control>
                          <Form.Label className="!mb-0">
                            {t(labelKey)}
                          </Form.Label>
                        </div>
                      </Form.Item>
                    )
                  }}
                />
              )
            })}
            <Hint>{t("products.duplicate.include.hint")}</Hint>
          </div>
        </RouteDrawer.Body>
        <RouteDrawer.Footer>
          <div className="flex items-center justify-end gap-x-2">
            <RouteDrawer.Close asChild>
              <Button size="small" variant="secondary">
                {t("actions.cancel")}
              </Button>
            </RouteDrawer.Close>
            <Button size="small" type="submit" isLoading={isPending}>
              {t("actions.duplicate")}
            </Button>
          </div>
        </RouteDrawer.Footer>
      </KeyboundForm>
    </RouteDrawer.Form>
  )
}
EOF
```

```bash
        it("copies every group when include is omitted", async () => {

        })

        it("copies every group for an empty include", async () => {
          const copy = (await duplicate({})).data.product

          expect(copy.images).toHaveLength(1)
          expect(copy.variants).toHaveLength(2)
        })

        it("copies no images when images are not selected", async () => {
          const copy = (await duplicate({ images: false })).data.product

          expect(copy.images ?? []).toHaveLength(0)
          // The other groups are untouched.
          expect(copy.variants).toHaveLength(2)
        })

        // copy keeps them even with no variants to use them.
        it("copies no variants but keeps options when variants are not selected", async () => {

          expect(copy.status).toEqual("draft")
```

```text
===== pr-97 (most recent, Sprint 3 format) =====
Closes #97

What: Adds a promotion CSV export. The Promotions list has an Export action next to Import. It opens a drawer, and confirming starts a background export of every promotion matching the list's current filters and search. The file uses the promotion import's columns, so an exported file can be imported again.

Why: Promotions could be imported but not exported, so there was no way to review them in a spreadsheet, keep a backup, or move them to another store. My spec review and the answers to the issue's open questions are on #97.

How: It follows the customer export file for file: a step that pages through promotions with an id cursor and streams the CSV to the File Module, a workflow that runs the step in the background and sends a feed notification on success or failure, `POST /admin/promotions/export` returning 202 with a transaction ID, an SDK method, and the Export action on the list.

The one deliberate difference is that the row conversion stays in `export-promotions.ts`, where the first commits on this branch put it, instead of living inside the step as the customer version does. The step imports `normalizePromotionForExport` and `EXPORT_COLUMNS` from there. The columns come from the import's own `COLUMNS` map rather than a second copy of the list, so the two can't drift when a column is added later.

Rules go out in the import's `attribute:operator:value1|value2` form, booleans as `true` and `false`, and anything the promotion doesn't have as an empty cell. A rule with no readable values is left out rather than written in a form the import would reject. The Export link carries the list's query string, which is how the drawer reads the same filters the list is showing.

The header is a literal in both tests, written from the list in AC3, not read from the code |

The integration test asserts the file's raw text, because the CSV reader coerces `false` and `10` back to a boolean and a number |

The expected `CreatePromotionDTO` is written out by hand from the source promotion, not captured from a run. For the last two, the expected result is AC6's own wording: no errors, and the promotion comes back with the rules that were readable |
| AC7: the export runs in the background, the route returns 202 with a `transaction_id`, and a notification carries the download link | `promotion-export.spec.ts`, in the `exportPromotions` helper every test goes through: it asserts the 202, the transaction ID, and the feed notification with the CSV's URL and `text/csv` type | integration | AC |

Not tested automatically, and why: nothing is manual-only. One gap worth naming though: I have not clicked the Export action in a running dashboard, so AC1 and AC2 are covered at the component level by the href and the request the drawer sends, not end to end in a browser.

AI-written tests: the step, workflow, route, drawer and all the tests on this branch were drafted with Claude Code. No expected value was copied from the output of code this PR adds, with one deliberate exception noted under Tech Debt. The headers and rule strings come from AC3 and AC4, the round trip's expected result is written out from the source promotion by hand, and the two exact CSV rows in the integration test were written from AC3's column order plus AC4 and AC5's formatting rules before the test was run; both matched on the first run.

Three of the tests on the export helper came from running a mutation tool over it rather than from reading the ACs again: an empty `Code` cell, a rule missing its attribute or operator, and a rule whose only value is blank. Two of them kill mutants nothing else caught. Dropping the `!rule.attribute` guard from `serializeRules` was failed by only the new rule test, and letting `code` fall through as `undefined` instead of an empty cell was failed by only the new code test. The third overlaps a test that already existed. I checked each by making the change and watching which tests failed.

Two things I had to correct. My first integration assertions expected `Automatic` to be the string `"false"` and `Discount Value` the string `"10"`, and the test failed: `csv2json` coerces those back to a boolean and a number when it reads the file, so a parsed row can never show how a value was written. The test now asserts the raw file text for AC5, which is what the criterion is actually about. Separately, the typecheck caught `useExportPromotions` taking a `query` argument it never used; it now passes it to the SDK the way `useExportCustomers` does.
```

yarn workspace @medusajs/core-flows test -- promotion/helpers
yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard test
yarn build, then with Postgres on 5433: cd integration-tests/http && DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5433 DB_USERNAME=postgres DB_PASSWORD=postgres npx jest __tests__/promotions/ (use your own DB_PORT)
